question: According to the NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, motorcycle helmets worn by operators and passengers must be approved under which federal safety standard?
choice_a: USDOT Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 218 (FMVSS 218)
explanation: The manual states that all motorcycle operators and passengers must wear approved motorcycle helmets as defined by USDOT Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (section 218).
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Special Rules and Required Equipment' section

question: To improve rider visibility, the manual recommends that motorcycle helmets have how much reflective material on both sides?
explanation: To improve the visibility of the motorcyclist, the manual recommends that helmets have at least four square inches of reflective material on both sides.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Special Rules and Required Equipment' section

question: Under New York's motorcycle equipment rules, when is a motorcycle operator required to wear approved eye protection?
choice_a: Only if the motorcycle does not have a windshield
choice_c: At all times, even if the motorcycle has a windshield
explanation: The manual states that all motorcycle operators must wear approved eye protection even if the motorcycle has a windshield, and any windshield must also be of an approved type.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Special Rules and Required Equipment' section

question: The eye protection worn by a motorcycle operator must conform to regulations established under which standard?
choice_b: New York State Vehicle and Traffic Law Section 402
choice_c: Society of Automotive Engineers standard SAE J1
choice_d: American National Standards Institute standard ANSI Z87.1
explanation: The manual states that eye protection must be made in a way that conforms with the regulations established by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI - Z87.1).
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Special Rules and Required Equipment' section

question: According to the manual, when must a motorcycle's headlight and rear light be turned on?
choice_a: At all times while operating on the road
explanation: The manual states that the headlight and rear light of the motorcycle must be on at all times when you operate on the road.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Special Rules and Required Equipment' section

question: Which of the following is true about how motorcyclists may position themselves within a lane, according to the manual?
choice_a: A motorcyclist must always ride single file at least one full lane width behind other traffic
choice_b: A motorcyclist can use a full lane and can ride two abreast with another motorcycle in the same lane
choice_c: A motorcyclist may ride between two lanes of traffic if necessary to pass
choice_d: A motorcyclist may only use half of a lane so that a car can share the lane
explanation: The manual states that motorcyclists can use a full lane and can ride two abreast in a single lane.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Special Rules and Required Equipment' section

question: Which riding position is prohibited for motorcyclists under New York's special rules?
choice_a: Riding two motorcycles abreast in a single lane
choice_b: Using the full width of a single lane
choice_c: Riding abreast of another vehicle in the same lane, between lanes, or between traffic and parked cars
choice_d: Riding in the right-hand portion of a lane
explanation: The manual states that a motorcyclist cannot ride abreast of another vehicle in the same lane, between lanes, or between traffic and parked cars.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Special Rules and Required Equipment' section

question: Regarding traffic laws, how does the manual describe motorcyclists' obligations for turns and lane changes?
choice_a: Motorcyclists are exempt from signaling because of their smaller size
choice_b: Motorcyclists only need to signal when riding with a passenger
choice_c: Motorcyclists may pass on the right regardless of lane markings
choice_d: Motorcyclists are subject to all rules of the road, including signals for all turns and lane changes, and may pass only where it is allowed for other vehicles
explanation: The manual states that motorcyclists are subject to all rules of the road, which includes signals for all turns and lane changes and passing only where it is allowed for other vehicles.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Special Rules and Required Equipment' section

question: According to the 'Children As Passengers' section, what are the age and helmet requirements for a child riding as a motorcycle passenger in New York?
choice_a: A child of any age may be a passenger, but must wear a DOT-approved motorcycle helmet and ride on a permanent passenger seat
choice_b: A child must be at least 5 years old and may wear a bicycle helmet
choice_c: A child must be at least 8 years old and wear a DOT-approved helmet
choice_d: Children under 12 are not permitted as motorcycle passengers
explanation: The manual states that a child of any age can be a motorcycle passenger in New York State, but every passenger must wear a DOT-approved motorcycle helmet and ride upon a permanent seat that can carry more than one person.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Children As Passengers' section

question: How must a child passenger be positioned on a motorcycle, according to the manual, unless seated in a sidecar?
choice_a: Facing forward, with both legs on the same side of the motorcycle
choice_b: Facing forward, with one leg on each side of the motorcycle and each foot on a foot peg
choice_c: Facing the rear, holding onto the operator
choice_d: Seated sideways with feet resting on the operator's seat
explanation: The manual states the passenger must sit facing forward, with one leg on each side of the motorcycle, and each foot on a foot peg, unless he or she is seated in a properly attached sidecar.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Children As Passengers' section

question: What does the manual say about a passenger's riding position that interferes with the operator's control of the motorcycle or vision?
choice_a: It is allowed as long as the passenger is an adult
choice_b: It is allowed only on motorcycles with sidecars
choice_c: It is illegal for the operator to carry, or the passenger to ride, in such a position
choice_d: It is legal if the trip is under one mile
explanation: The manual states it is illegal for an operator to carry a passenger, or for the passenger to ride, in a position that will interfere with the operation or control of the motorcycle or the vision of the operator.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Children As Passengers' section

question: Under New York's required-equipment rules, which motorcycles must be equipped with directional (turn) signals?
choice_a: All motorcycles regardless of model year
choice_b: Only motorcycles used on interstate highways
choice_d: Motorcycles originally equipped with turn signals, or those that are 1985 or newer models
explanation: The manual requires directional signals if the motorcycle was originally equipped with turn signals or is a 1985 or newer model; it also separately requires brakes on both wheels for 1971 and newer motorcycles.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Special Rules and Required Equipment' section

question: Which of the following is part of New York's required motorcycle equipment list?
choice_a: A horn or other warning device, at least one mirror, a suitable muffler without cutouts or removable baffles, and handlebars no higher than the operator's shoulder height
choice_b: Two mirrors, one on each handlebar, mandatory
choice_c: A muffler with a cutout permitted for racing use
choice_d: Handlebars no higher than the operator's head height
explanation: The manual requires a horn or other warning device, at least one mirror mounted on a handlebar (though mirrors on both are recommended), a suitable muffler with cutouts or removable baffles prohibited, and handlebars no higher than the shoulder height of the operator.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Special Rules and Required Equipment' section
